title: The Jensen Scandal Is Much Worse Than It Looks
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
source_note: Captions garble names (Huang/Wang rendered 'Wong', Mega Speed as 'Megape'/'Megaspe', Hakeem Jeffries as 'Hakee Jeff').
summary: Joseph Carlson opens with the news that Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has admitted an extramarital affair with Alice Wang (rendered 'Wong' in the auto-captions), a former Chinese state-media reporter who later led Mega Speed International, a Singapore-based cloud provider US authorities are investigating as a possible backdoor for funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI chips to China. Huang disclosed the affair to Nvidia's board and emailed all employees apologising and taking full responsibility. Carlson calls the apology sincere, but argues it matters to investors because they back Nvidia partly on Huang's judgment and credibility, and the affair cuts against his image of long-term discipline and emotional stability. Carlson stresses the complication: Wang is not a random person — he cites New York Times reporting that US intelligence agencies identified her as passing information to Beijing, and Mega Speed's business is dispersing Nvidia GPUs through China and Asia. He expects major investigations, congressional hearings and possibly tighter AI and chip-export regulation under the incoming Democratic Congress. On the stock, NVDA is down about 4.6–5.4% on the day to around $176 from $240; Carlson says he is 'not so concerned', the stock is already cheap and sold off, he cannot see it dumping much more, and investors may treat the scandal as a buying opportunity — though he makes no explicit buy recommendation himself. He closes with a 'fail of the week' on Scott Galloway admitting he defecated in his Tesla's passenger seat to spite Elon Musk, which Carlson calls deranged. No explicit stock call; NVDA discussed at length, TSLA mentioned only in passing.
